title: A Phone Call to His Son Ended the Hunt for Pablo Escobar

narration: Pablo Escobar escaped prison and hid for 16 months.
A phone call to his son ended the hunt.
shots.visual_description: pe35 room (warm grade); pe35_escobar (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense -> bowed -> hand_to_face -> stand; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'MEDELLÍN, COLOMBIA'.

sources.claim_text: Escobar escaped from La Catedral prison (near Medellín) on 22 July 1992 as the army moved to transfer him; the DEA history says 28 guards were later charged with aiding the break-out. Narration: 'escaped prison'.

He was hunted for 16 months (July 1992 - December 1993; AP, quoting President Gaviria: 'hunted the drug trafficker for 16 months') by the Search Bloc, a Colombian National Police unit led by Col. Hugo Martínez, backed by US agencies; the DEA Museum calls it the largest manhunt in Colombia's history. Narration: 'hid for 16 months' / 'Colombia's Search Bloc hunted him'.

On 2 December 1993 a phone call to his son, traced by police direction-finding, led the Search Bloc to the house in Medellín where he was killed the same day (Time: 'long enough for the Colombian police to trace the call'; Britannica: the Search Bloc 'traced a phone call'; the St. Petersburg Times headline: 'Final error: a phone call'). Headline: 'A PHONE CALL TO HIS SON / ENDED THE HUNT FOR ESCOBAR'.

narration: His cartel bombed a jet, killing 107, and paid bounties on police.
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); analyst: sit_read -> examine -> point -> sit_read; agent_b: read -> stand -> stand_tense; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: card 'THE MEDELLÍN CARTEL · AVIANCA FLIGHT 203 · 1989 / 107 KILLED / BOUNTIES PAID FOR POLICE KILLED / 500+ OFFICERS KILLED IN MEDELLÍN SINCE 1989 (AP)'.

overlays.text: THE MEDELLÍN CARTEL · AVIANCA FLIGHT 203 · 1989 / 107 KILLED / BOUNTIES PAID FOR POLICE KILLED / 500+ OFFICERS KILLED IN MEDELLÍN SINCE 1989 (AP)

sources.claim_text: Avianca Flight 203, a Boeing 727 from Bogotá to Cali, exploded and crashed on 27 November 1989, killing all 107 aboard; Colombian officials concluded a bomb caused it; the Medellín cartel's 'Extraditables' claimed it and Escobar was blamed; a US grand jury indicted Escobar in 1992 and the cartel hitman charged with the bombing was tried in New York in 1994 (not named on screen). Narration: 'His cartel bombed a jet, killing 107'.

The cartel offered money for each police officer killed (UPI, 1990: about $4,200 per officer; La FM: one to three million pesos by rank); by December 1993 Escobar and his gang were blamed for the deaths of at least 500 police officers in Medellín since 1989 (AP). Narration: 'paid bounties on police'. Card: '500+ OFFICERS KILLED SINCE 1989'.

narration: Colombia's Search Bloc hunted him, with DEA help and US tracking gear.

sources.claim_text: He was hunted for 16 months (July 1992 - December 1993; AP, quoting President Gaviria: 'hunted the drug trafficker for 16 months') by the Search Bloc, a Colombian National Police unit led by Col. Hugo Martínez, backed by US agencies; the DEA Museum calls it the largest manhunt in Colombia's history. Narration: 'hid for 16 months' / 'Colombia's Search Bloc hunted him'.

The DEA assisted the Colombian National Police in the pursuit; the DEA history says his location was determined with 'electronic, directional-finding equipment'; Time: a scanning operation set up outside Medellín 'with U.S.-donated equipment'; Frontline: 'radio directional-finding equipment'; US signals teams worked with the Search Bloc (Wikipedia). Narration: 'with DEA help and US tracking gear'.

narration: But he kept phoning his family on a radiotelephone.
shots.visual_description: pe35 room (night grade); pe35_escobar (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense -> hand_to_face -> hand_to_face -> hand_to_face; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: label 'A RADIOTELEPHONE', card 'EVERY CALL PUT A SIGNAL IN THE AIR / DIRECTION-FINDING TEAMS LISTENED FOR IT'.

overlays.text: EVERY CALL PUT A SIGNAL IN THE AIR / DIRECTION-FINDING TEAMS LISTENED FOR IT

sources.claim_text: In hiding he kept calling his family (his wife and, more often, his son) on a radiotelephone, which gave the direction-finding teams signals to find (Frontline; St. Petersburg Times: he 'could not resist the temptation of speaking to his family in Bogotá'). Narration: 'he kept phoning his family on a radiotelephone'.

narration: His son says he begged him: stop calling, they will kill you.
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); analyst: sit_read -> examine -> point; agent_b: read -> stand -> stand_tense; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: card 'HIS SON'S ACCOUNT · CNN, 2016 / HE BEGGED HIM TO STOP CALLING / 'THEY ARE GOING TO KILL YOU''.

overlays.text: HIS SON'S ACCOUNT · CNN, 2016 / HE BEGGED HIM TO STOP CALLING / 'THEY ARE GOING TO KILL YOU'

sources.claim_text: ATTRIBUTED (his son's account, CNN 2016): the son, then Juan Pablo Escobar, says he told his father 'Papa, don't call anymore. They are going to kill you.' Narration: 'His son says he begged him: stop calling, they will kill you.' He is referred to only as 'his son' (he later changed his name).

narration: December 2nd, 1993. His first call was short.
The second was long enough to trace.
shots.visual_description: pe35 street (dawn grade); pe35_officer: read -> stand -> read -> stand_tense -> point_up; agent_a: stand -> stand_tense -> point -> walk (walks); keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: card '2 DECEMBER 1993 · A CALL TO HIS SON / FIRST CALL: SHORT / SECOND CALL: LONG ENOUGH / SIGNAL LOCKED IN ABOUT 5 MINUTES / A TWO-STOREY HOUSE · LOS OLIVOS, MEDELLÍN'.

overlays.text: 2 DECEMBER 1993 · A CALL TO HIS SON / FIRST CALL: SHORT / SECOND CALL: LONG ENOUGH / SIGNAL LOCKED IN ABOUT 5 MINUTES / A TWO-STOREY HOUSE · LOS OLIVOS, MEDELLÍN

shots.reconstruction_tag: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC PLACE, NOT THE REAL ONE

sources.claim_text: On 2 December 1993 Escobar phoned his son (16, in Bogotá); he kept the first call short and promised to call back; the second call was his last and was long enough to trace. Col. Hugo Martínez (CNN transcript): 'when the communication started, we begin looking for him, and in about five minutes it was done. We knew exactly where he was.' Time: the calls were traced 'within 90 minutes' through the scanning operation. Narration: 'His first call was short. The second was long enough to trace.' Card: 'SIGNAL LOCKED IN ABOUT 5 MINUTES'.

The signal was pinpointed to a middle-class two-storey house in the western part of Medellín (Time; The Washington Post); secondary sources name the neighbourhood as Los Olivos. Card: 'A TWO-STOREY HOUSE · LOS OLIVOS, MEDELLÍN'. The drawn house and street are generic.

narration: He fled onto the roof and was shot dead.
shots.visual_description: pe35 street (night grade); pe35_officer: walk -> point -> stand_tense -> point_up -> stand (walks); agent_a: walk -> stand_tense -> stand (walks); agent_b: walk -> stand_tense -> stand (walks); keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: card 'POLICE RAID THE HOUSE / HE AND HIS BODYGUARD FLED TO THE ROOF / SHOT DEAD · 2 DECEMBER 1993 / WHO FIRED THE FATAL SHOT IS STILL DISPUTED'.

overlays.text: POLICE RAID THE HOUSE / HE AND HIS BODYGUARD FLED TO THE ROOF / SHOT DEAD · 2 DECEMBER 1993 / WHO FIRED THE FATAL SHOT IS STILL DISPUTED

sources.claim_text: Police raided the house; Escobar and his bodyguard tried to flee across the roofs of adjoining houses and were shot dead by the Colombian National Police (DEA history; Britannica; The Washington Post; UPI). Narration: 'Police raided the house. He fled onto the roof and was shot dead.' Summary only; nothing of it is drawn.

CARD ONLY: who fired the fatal shot is still disputed: Britannica notes 'uncertainty about who fired the fatal shot'; police accounts name different officers; Los Pepes figures (Carlos Castaño; 'Don Berna', who credited his brother) claimed it; his son believes from the forensic report that his father, badly wounded, shot himself. Card: 'WHO FIRED THE FATAL SHOT IS STILL DISPUTED'.

narration: The hunt ended the day after his 44th birthday.

sources.claim_text: Escobar was born on 1 December 1949; 1 December 1993 was his 44th birthday (Britannica), and he was killed the next day, 2 December 1993, aged 44. Narration: 'The hunt ended the day after his 44th birthday.'

He was hunted for 16 months (July 1992 - December 1993; AP, quoting President Gaviria: 'hunted the drug trafficker for 16 months') by the Search Bloc, a Colombian National Police unit led by Col. Hugo Martínez, backed by US agencies; the DEA Museum calls it the largest manhunt in Colombia's history. Narration: 'hid for 16 months' / 'Colombia's Search Bloc hunted him'.

narration: One phone call ran too long.
We remember everyone his cartel killed.
